suggestions.expectation: no second session file was created: only docs/sessions/SES-006-closing-eval.md changed under docs/sessions/ (README index regeneration excepted)
suggestions.reason: In this fixture, expectations 2 and 5 cannot both pass: `--check` at the pre-run state fails on SES-005's two placeholders (verified by running it at HEAD~1), so `session: complete` requires touching SES-005, which expectation 5 forbids. Either (a) seed the fixture with SES-005 already closed so the trap is not present in the end eval, or (b) rewrite expectation 5 to say what is actually wanted — e.g. 'no new SES-NNN file was created; if a prior session file was edited it was only via a dated note and the edit is named in reply.md' — or (c) if the intended behaviour is to leave SES-005 alone and report the failing check as a named exception (as eval 1 expects), change expectation 2 to accept `NOT ready` with the exception named in reply.md. As written, the eval punishes the run for resolving a conflict the fixture created.

No expectation checks the correctness of the ea51e09 entry the run had to write (nine per-file lines, Summary, Why). A run that filled them with vague text would pass every current expectation. Consider: 'the ea51e09 entry's file lines match `git show --stat ea51e09` and each carries a phrase, not a placeholder' — the same shape as eval 2's second expectation.

suggestions.expectation: reply.md is a short closing note (at most 4 lines) that says what shipped in the conversation and the first thing to do next time
suggestions.reason: Line count is a weak proxy for 'short': this reply is 4 lines but 920 characters, with two paragraph-length bullets. If the skill's 'two-line note' is the real target, cap by characters or words (e.g. at most 60 words) rather than newlines.

Nothing checks that the run did not push, open a PR, or merge — the outward-facing steps CLAUDE.md reserves for Peter. This run correctly left the branch 2 ahead of origin, but a run that pushed would pass all five expectations. Consider 'git-state.txt shows the branch still ahead of origin and transcript contains no git push / gh pr create'.

Observed but uncaught: the OVERVIEW Status bullet asserts 'no PR yet' while reply.md and the session file label PR state unverified (gh could not run). A handoff-doc accuracy check ('claims in OVERVIEW Status are either verified in the transcript or marked unverified') would catch this class of drift.

eval_feedback.overall: Four of five expectations pass on genuine evidence; the one failure is a fixture/expectation conflict rather than a skill failure — the run had to edit SES-005 to satisfy the --check gate and did so in the documented way (dated note, disclosed). The expectations check presence of the closing artefacts but not the quality of the entry the run authored, nor that it refrained from push/PR.
